key_insight: PE-EK-PINN turns converged physics solutions into reusable evolved kernels, letting large wave systems be built hierarchically without manually deriving new physics terms at every scale.
engineering_relevance: This makes physics-informed neural networks more practical for large electromagnetic configurations such as antenna arrays and metasurfaces by cutting training cost and keeping the active kernel set small.
method: Embed physics through oscillatory kernels plus learnable envelopes.
Freeze a solved subsystem field and promote it to an evolved kernel.
Reuse transformed kernel copies to model higher-level structures with logarithmic cost growth.
evidence_signal: On dipole arrays, composite line-source geometries, and cross arrays, the method reduced training cost while achieving reduced or comparable relative L2 error; one 256-dipole array case trained more than 30× faster than direct PE-PINN.
watch_item: The approach depends on successfully converging and freezing lower-level subsystems, so training stability and kernel reuse quality may become a bottleneck in more complex or poorly conditioned geometries.
paper_title: PE-EK-PINN: Physics Embedding with Evolving Kernel for Scalable Physics-Informed Neural Networks
